message.content: Comments in this codebase use lowercase with square-bracket annotations to enforce strict machine-parseability and tooling interoperability. The lowercase requirement eliminates case-sensitivity noise, ensuring deterministic behavior across locales and environments where comment parsing tools operate. Square-bracket annotations (`[type: description]`) provide a structured, regex-friendly interface that allows automated systems to extract metadata, generate documentation, perform static analysis, and validate intent without ambiguity. This convention also prevents accidental interference with string literals or variable names, since square brackets are not valid identifiers in most programming languages, and lowercase avoids shadowing any potential identifier collision. Together, these constraints create a zero-overhead contract between human readers and machine consumers, making the codebase both human-readable and programmatically consumable without additional parsing layers.
